text: Android: OverviewViewModelTest is flaky (MainDispatcherRule / runTest dispatcher race)

Partially fixed: MainDispatcherRule.dispatcher made public so tests awaiting multiple sequential async calls can share it via runTest(mainDispatcherRule.dispatcher), fixing the SettingsViewModelTest race (commit a6fcc7a). OverviewViewModelTest still flakes with the same TestMainDispatcher-class error (IllegalStateException / UncompletedCoroutinesError) -- it hasn't been converted to the shared-dispatcher pattern yet. Broader fix (auditing every runTest{} call site across the suite, or a more systemic solution) still open.

New sighting during T-63's full-suite verification: ItemFormViewModelTest (add/edit item dialog VM, unrelated code to T-63) hit the same TestMainDispatcher.kt IllegalStateException race as OverviewViewModelTest -- confirmed via an isolated re-run passing cleanly, so it's the same resource-contention-sensitive dual-scheduler issue, not a new bug. Still open: the broader fix (auditing/converting every runTest{} call site across the suite to share MainDispatcherRule.dispatcher, or a more systemic solution) hasn't been done.

Applied the ticket's literally-suggested fix broadly: converted all ~115 runTest{} call sites across the 10 MainDispatcherRule-using test files to runTest(mainDispatcherRule.dispatcher){}, so every test now shares one TestCoroutineScheduler with Dispatchers.Main instead of two independent ones. Commit a6eb178. This is real, verified, non-regressing progress -- but it does NOT fully close the ticket.

New, more precise diagnosis found via full-suite runs after the fix: the actual exception is 'IllegalStateException: Dispatchers.Main is used concurrently with setting it' from kotlinx-coroutines-test's TestMainDispatcher$NonConcurrentlyModifiable guard -- a genuine cross-thread race on the single global Dispatchers.Main, not (only) the within-test dual-scheduler issue originally diagnosed. Root cause: Robolectric's SandboxTestRunner executes test bodies on its own ThreadPoolExecutor sandbox threads (visible in the stack trace), and UnconfinedTestDispatcher's eager cross-thread resumption means a coroutine from test N can still be touching Dispatchers.Main on a background thread just as test N+1's MainDispatcherRule.starting() reinstalls it. Confirmed via isolated re-runs: ItemFormViewModelTest's 'an invalid price is rejected inline' and ListViewModelTest's A10 test -- both failed in a full-suite run, both passed cleanly every time in isolation -- ruling out a bug in those tests' own logic.

Still open: full elimination needs either (a) migrating MainDispatcherRule's default from UnconfinedTestDispatcher to StandardTestDispatcher (large: many of the ~115 call sites currently rely on Unconfined's eager execution and would need explicit advanceUntilIdle() calls added, high regression risk), or (b) explicit cancellation of every ViewModel's long-lived coroutine scope (combine/collect on flows that never complete) between tests, or (c) some other mechanism not yet identified. This is a genuine architectural tradeoff, not a mechanical fix -- deferred pending a decision on which direction to take.

FIXED and verified. Root cause was more precise than the original diagnosis: never-cancelled ViewModel Room-flow collectors running on real Dispatchers.IO threads posted to the single global Dispatchers.Main at the next test's setMain, tripping kotlinx-coroutines-test's concurrent-modification guard ('Dispatchers.Main is used concurrently with setting it'). UnconfinedTestDispatcher's eager cross-thread resumption amplified it. Fix (commit c8b8b28, building on a6eb178): (1) MainDispatcherRule -> StandardTestDispatcher (confines Main-dispatched execution to the single test thread), (2) routed Room's query coroutine context in all 8 rule-based ViewModelTests from Dispatchers.IO to the shared mainDispatcherRule.dispatcher (removes the last real background threads). Everything now runs single-threaded on one scheduler. No stale-state breakage (tests already await via job.join()/uiState.first{}). Verified with 4 consecutive genuine --rerun full-suite runs, all BUILD SUCCESSFUL -- the flake was full-suite-load/timing dependent and always passed in isolation, so repeated full runs were the meaningful check. Lint clean.
